canonicalExplanation.summary: **Progressive enhancement** means building in layers: first a solid **HTML baseline** where the core content and tasks work (readable text, working links, submittable forms); then **CSS** for layout and looks; then **JavaScript** for extras. If a layer fails — slow network, blocked script, old device — the layers below still work. It doesn't mean every fancy feature must work without JS; it means the **core** does, and you document what degrades.

sections.heading: Start here
sections.body:
A learner on a train opens your course catalogue. The JavaScript bundle times out. Do they see a blank page with a spinner — or a list of courses they can still click? A server-rendered course list remains readable and linked before JavaScript adds filtering and saved progress. In this lesson you'll demonstrate the site with styles and scripts unavailable and document acceptable degradation.

sections.heading: Document the degradation

includes: Build a baseline where core content and tasks work without CSS and JavaScript.
Test with styles and scripts disabled and document acceptable degradation.

outcomes: Demonstrate the site with styles and scripts unavailable and document acceptable degradation.

examples.title: A course list before and after JavaScript
examples.situation: A server-rendered course list remains readable and linked before JavaScript adds filtering and saved progress.
walkthrough: **Server-rendered course list:** the HTML contains every course as a real link, readable with no CSS.
**Baseline filter:** a GET form lets the server filter the list; JavaScript will later replace it with instant filtering.
**Test and document:** with JS disabled, the list remains readable and linked; the note says instant filtering and saved progress need JS.
examples.result: The core journey works on any connection, and the enhancements are documented as optional.

examples.title: The blank single-page app
examples.situation:
A catalogue page's HTML is just `
` and a 1 MB script. With the script blocked, the page is blank.
walkthrough: No content or links exist until JavaScript runs.
Search engines, slow devices and blocked scripts all see nothing.
Fix: render the course list and links in HTML on the server, then hydrate or enhance with JavaScript.
examples.result: Even without JavaScript, learners can find and open courses.

misconceptions.mistakenBelief: Progressive enhancement means every advanced interaction must work identically with JavaScript disabled.
misconceptions.correction: It means the core content and tasks work in the HTML baseline, while enhancements may depend on CSS or JavaScript — as long as their absence leaves an acceptable, documented experience.
misconceptions.diagnosticPrompt: In "A course list before and after JavaScript", which features were enhancements?

analogy.example: Progressive enhancement is like a **bicycle with an electric motor**: if the battery dies, you can still pedal home. A bike with no pedals — only the motor — strands you.
usefulFor: remembering the baseline must work alone
limitations: Bikes don't get documentation; your site's degradation notes should be written down.
Some rides (features) genuinely need the motor — that's fine if they're extras.

steps.explanation: A server-rendered course list is readable and linked before any script runs.

trace.textAlternative: Layering enhancements over an HTML baseline. Step 1, Baseline: course links is present in HTML; filter is server GET form. A server-rendered course list is readable and linked before any script runs. Step 2, Scripts unavailable: filtering is page reload; saved progress is unavailable. With JS disabled the core task still works, with documented degradation. Step 3, Enhanced: filtering is instant; saved progress is on. JavaScript adds filtering and saved progress on top of the baseline.

remediation.explanation: Name the page's **one core task**. Disable JS and CSS and try it. If it fails, move that part into HTML (links, forms, server rendering). Everything else is an enhancement to document.
